title: Remount
teaches: The remount as we trade it: a leader loses a line for real, an average or a price level it held, then retakes it with a clear green close. We buy after a quiet day holds above the line, with a market order over that day's high and a real stop a few cents under its low. The close must be above the 200-day, a third comes off at 3R and 5R, and most tries lose small.

questions.q: In one line, what is a Remount?
choices: Retaking a line the stock really lost
A one-day dip under yesterday's low
A gap up over resistance on earnings
A breakout from a flat base on volume
questions.answer: Retaking a line the stock really lost
questions.why: Retaking a line the stock really lost. A Remount lost the 50-day or 200-day for real and is buying it back.
questions.lesson_line: A Remount is a line lost for real, then taken back.

wrong.A one-day dip under yesterday's low: That is an Oops, one session. A Remount follows a real loss of a line.
wrong.A gap up over resistance on earnings: A gap is a catalyst setup. A Remount buys back a lost line.
wrong.A breakout from a flat base on volume: A flat base breakout trades through a ceiling. A Remount retakes a line it lost.

questions.q: The Remount has two kinds of line: a moving average, and a price level that held.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The average form is the 50-day or the 200-day. The level form is a pivot, base low, old high or round number the stock held before it broke.
questions.lesson_line: One setup, two kinds of line: an average or a level.

questions.q: Which averages does the moving-average form use?
choices: The 50-day and the 200-day
The 5-day and the 8-day lines
The 10-week and the 30-week lines
The session VWAP
questions.answer: The 50-day and the 200-day
questions.why: The 50-day and the 200-day. If the stock lost and retook one of them, it is the moving-average form.
questions.lesson_line: Fifty or two hundred. Those are the lines.

wrong.The 5-day and the 8-day lines: Those are too short to count as a lost line. The Remount uses the 50-day and 200-day.
wrong.The 10-week and the 30-week lines: Those are weekly lines. Ours are the 50-day and the 200-day.
wrong.The session VWAP: VWAP resets every day. A lost line has to be one the stock sat under for days.

questions.q: You may buy a Remount before the close is above the line to get a better price.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Wait for the close. Buying before the close is above the line, or on a marginal poke a few cents over it, is a listed mistake.
questions.lesson_line: No close above the line, no Remount. Do not anticipate.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The remount close must be above the ___-day SMA.
questions.why: 200. The remount close is above the 200-day SMA, and a 200-day remount is the cross itself. No longs below the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: Above the 200-day, every time.

questions.q: A Remount buy is a limit order, and the stop is a real order with the broker.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Entries are market orders, and every position has a real stop order with the broker, not a stop kept in your head.
questions.lesson_line: Market order in, real stop order out.

questions.q: A successful Remount turns the line from a ceiling back into a floor.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The stock lost the line and it became a ceiling. A clean retake makes it support again.
questions.lesson_line: Ceiling to floor. That is the whole idea.

questions.q: A 50-day reclaim counts only if the close is also above the 200-day.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A 50-day reclaim counts only with the close above the 200-day too. ChartSchool agrees: with price above the 200-day, focus on the 50-day signals.
questions.lesson_line: A fifty-day retake needs the 200-day under you first.

questions.q: What does IBD say institutions may do once a stock is below its 50-day?
choices: Use the line to mark a sell level
Buy every dip to the line
Ignore the line until the 200-day
Short only above the line
questions.answer: Use the line to mark a sell level
questions.why: Use the line to mark a sell level. That is why it takes a large boost of buying power to muscle back above it.
questions.lesson_line: Lost lines turn into sell levels. Retaking one takes real buying.

wrong.Buy every dip to the line: IBD says the opposite: below the line it can mark a sell level.
wrong.Ignore the line until the 200-day: IBD treats the 50-day line as a level institutions watch.
wrong.Short only above the line: IBD speaks of a sell level under the line, not a short rule.

questions.q: A Remount counts once price pokes a few cents over the line during the day.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. A remount needs a full candle close above the average. A marginal poke a few cents over the line is not a remount day.
questions.lesson_line: Close it above. A poke is not a retake.

questions.q: IBD reads a weak, low-volume rise after a high-volume drop under the 50-day as what?
choices: A chance to sell
A Remount to buy
A reason to add
A confirmed bottom
questions.answer: A chance to sell
questions.why: A chance to sell. A high-volume decline to or below the 50-day followed by a weak low-volume rise is your chance to sell.
questions.lesson_line: A light drift back after a heavy drop is a sell, not a buy.

wrong.A Remount to buy: IBD says the opposite. A light rise after a heavy drop is a sell, and our card lists it as a mistake.
wrong.A reason to add: A weak rise gives no reason to add.
wrong.A confirmed bottom: A weak, low-volume rise confirms nothing.

questions.q: A Remount on the earnings reaction day is allowed, because the report is already out.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A remount on the earnings gap itself is after the report and allowed. AMD remounted its 50-day on the reaction day.
questions.lesson_line: After the report is fine. Before it is not.

questions.q: What most separates a Remount from a U&R?
choices: How long the line stayed lost
The color of the candle
The ticker's sector
The size of the first volume bar
questions.answer: How long the line stayed lost
questions.why: How long the line stayed lost. A U&R closes back above within 3 sessions. A Remount spent far longer under the line.
questions.lesson_line: Count the sessions under the line. A quick return is a U&R, a long stay a Remount.

wrong.The color of the candle: Both setups end on a strong close. The stay under the line is what differs.
wrong.The ticker's sector: Sector does not tell the setups apart.
wrong.The size of the first volume bar: Volume can be heavy in either setup. The count of sessions under the line decides.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: Move the stop to breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first ___ by default.
questions.answer: trim
questions.why: Trim. The stop goes to breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default.
questions.lesson_line: First trim, stop to breakeven.

questions.q: Buy 101.19, stop 99.98. How far is the stop below the buy, in percent?
questions.why: 1.2%. The buy minus the stop, divided by the buy. That is NKE: well inside the 3% the stop usually sits within.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the stop in percent before you size the trade.

questions.q: Bought at 109.42 with the stop at 105.86. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 120.10. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add three of those to the fill. The first third comes off there.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open.

questions.q: A close back under the line after the buy is an extra exit before the stop.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The stop is the exit. A close back under the line is not an extra exit; the trade is held while it stays above the stop.
questions.lesson_line: The stop is the exit. A close under the line is a warning only.

questions.q: What kind of stop do we place on a Remount?
choices: A broker order under the low
A close-only stop under the line
A mental stop at the line
No stop until 1R
questions.answer: A broker order under the low
questions.why: A broker order under the low. It is a real stop that only moves up.
questions.lesson_line: A real order, a few cents under the low.

wrong.A close-only stop under the line: A stop that waits for a close cannot sit with the broker as an order.
wrong.A mental stop at the line: Every position has a real stop order with the broker.
wrong.No stop until 1R: The stop goes in with the buy. It is never optional.

questions.q: A gap through the stop is this setup's main failure.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Chop around the line is the main failure, and the time stop frees the money. ChartSchool agrees that crossover signals are less reliable in sideways markets.
questions.lesson_line: Chop kills Remounts. The time stop frees the money.

questions.q: After the remount day, what arms the buy?
choices: A quiet inside day above the line
Any red day on heavy volume
A gap down under the line
A new 52-week low on heavy volume
questions.answer: A quiet inside day above the line
questions.why: A quiet inside day above the line. The pause closes above the line, and the buy is a market order as price trades over that day's high.
questions.lesson_line: Retake, pause, then buy over the quiet day's high.

wrong.Any red day on heavy volume: A red day proves nothing. The pause has to hold above the line and go quiet.
wrong.A gap down under the line: A close back under the line before the trigger means no trade.
wrong.A new 52-week low on heavy volume: A new low is the opposite of a retake.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.answer: up
questions.why: Up. The stop is the exit. It only moves up, never down or wider. The gap rule is the one exception.
questions.lesson_line: Up, never wider.

questions.q: A $9 stock that trades $30 million a day passes our price and volume rule for a Remount.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. We trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day. The volume passes and the price fails.
questions.lesson_line: Ten dollars and twenty million a day. Both.

questions.q: Is this a Remount?
choices: No; a pullback or U&R, line kept
Yes, it retook the 50-day cleanly
Yes, if the volume is heavy
Yes, buy the close
questions.answer: No; a pullback or U&R, line kept
questions.why: No. The line was never really lost, so it is a pullback or a U&R.
questions.lesson_line: A two-day dip is not a lost line.

wrong.Yes, it retook the 50-day cleanly: It retook the line, but the line was never really lost. Two sessions is a dip.
wrong.Yes, if the volume is heavy: Volume does not change the count. A short dip is not a lost line.
wrong.Yes, buy the close: Buying the close of a short dip is a pullback or U&R trade, with its own rules.

questions.story: A leader closes under its 50-day for two sessions. Then it closes back above with a strong candle.

questions.q: Which setup is this?
choices: The AVWAP reclaim
A moving-average Remount
A level Remount
An Oops
questions.answer: The AVWAP reclaim
questions.why: The AVWAP reclaim. A line that starts at one event day and bends with volume is the AVWAP; a Remount line is an average or a flat level.
questions.lesson_line: Name the line. A bending line from an event day is not a Remount.

wrong.A moving-average Remount: A Remount uses the 50-day or the 200-day, which do not start at one event day.
wrong.A level Remount: A level Remount uses a flat price level that held. This line bends with volume.
wrong.An Oops: An Oops is one session that opens under the prior close. It has no line like this.

questions.story: A stock closes over a line that starts at its August high and bends with volume.

questions.q: Bought at 59.54, stop 58.44. The stock trades to 61.47. How many R is that?
questions.why: 1.75R. Each R is the fill minus the stop. DOCU got that far inside its window without reaching 3R.
questions.lesson_line: Count in R. Under 3R, no trim.

questions.q: Given the wide stop, what is the call?
choices: Size down or skip; never tighten
Tighten the stop to fit a full size
Buy full size and accept the risk
Use the line on a close
questions.answer: Size down or skip; never tighten
questions.why: Size down or skip. If the stop is more than about 3% away, size down so the account risk is unchanged, or skip. Never tighten it to fit.
questions.lesson_line: A wide stop means fewer shares or no trade. Never tighten it.

wrong.Tighten the stop to fit a full size: Never tighten the stop to fit. A stop that does not mark the real low is not honest.
wrong.Buy full size and accept the risk: The size comes from the stop. A wide stop means fewer shares or no trade.
wrong.Use the line on a close: A stop on a close cannot sit with the broker, and it does not fix the distance.

questions.story: A clean Remount sets up. The honest stop, a few cents under the low, is 5.5% below the buy.

questions.q: Gap through the stop. Your move?
choices: Get out; that low is past 2R
Set the stop at 57.20 and hold
Keep the 58.44 stop and wait
Buy more at the lower price
questions.answer: Get out; that low is past 2R
questions.why: Get out. A gap through the stop hands it to the first 30-minute low, but if that takes the loss past 2R, get out.
questions.lesson_line: First 30 minutes decide. Past 2R, out.

wrong.Set the stop at 57.20 and hold: The first 30-minute low is the new stop, but only up to a ceiling. Past 2R, you are out.
wrong.Keep the 58.44 stop and wait: The stock is already through it. The gap rule hands the stop to the first 30 minutes.
wrong.Buy more at the lower price: No adding, and never into a gap against the stop.

questions.story: You bought at 59.54 with the stop at 58.44, so 1R is 1.10. The next morning gaps down to 57.80. The first 30-minute low is 57.20.

questions.q: The open is past your 3R level. Your move?
choices: Take the first third at the open
Wait for 104.82 on a pullback down
Hold it all and trail the average
Sell everything at the open
questions.answer: Take the first third at the open
questions.why: Take the first third at the open. If a stock opens above a trim level, take that trim at the open.
questions.lesson_line: Gap past a trim level: take it at the open.

wrong.Wait for 104.82 on a pullback down: You may never see it again. A trim level the day opens past is taken at the open.
wrong.Hold it all and trail the average: The trail is for the last third, after the trims.
wrong.Sell everything at the open: The plan is a third at 3R, a third at 5R, then the trail.

questions.story: You bought at 101.19 with the stop at 99.98. Your 3R level is 104.82. Two days later the stock opens at 106.00.

questions.q: Account 100,000, risk 0.5%. Buy 109.42, stop 105.86. How many shares does the stop allow?
questions.why: 140 shares. The size comes from the stop: risk divided by the distance, rounded down. The 40% position cap is not close. That stop was 3.3% from the buy.
questions.lesson_line: The stop sets the size. Wider stop, fewer shares.

questions.q: Which average trails a fresh 200-day remount?
choices: The 21-day, for a steadier name
The 3-day, for a fast mover
The 200-day, the line you retook
The 50-day, for any remount
questions.answer: The 21-day, for a steadier name
questions.why: The 21-day, for a steadier name. A fast mover trails the 10-day. Sell on a close below it.
questions.lesson_line: Steady name, 21-day. Fast mover, 10-day.

wrong.The 3-day, for a fast mover: That is far too tight and shakes you out of a runner.
wrong.The 200-day, the line you retook: The line you just retook is far too slow to trail.
wrong.The 50-day, for any remount: The card names the 21-day for a steadier name and the 10-day for a fast mover.

questions.q: What now?
choices: Sell; under 1R after 10 sessions
Hold, because the stop is not hit
Add to the position
Move the stop up to breakeven
questions.answer: Sell; under 1R after 10 sessions
questions.why: Sell. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold. Chop is this setup's main failure.
questions.lesson_line: Ten sessions, under 1R: out.

wrong.Hold, because the stop is not hit: The stop is not the only exit. A trade still under 1R after 10 sessions is sold.
wrong.Add to the position: We do not add. The money is better used on a new setup.
wrong.Move the stop up to breakeven: Breakeven comes at 2R to 5R, not at 0.5R.

questions.story: Ten sessions after the buy, the stock sits at 0.5R. The stop has not been hit and no trim has come off.

questions.q: Where do the first two trims come off?
choices: A third at 3R, a third at 5R
Half at 2R, half at 4R
All of it at 3R
A third each at 1R, 2R and 3R
questions.answer: A third at 3R, a third at 5R
questions.why: A third at 3R and another third at 5R, then trail the last third.
questions.lesson_line: Third at 3R, third at 5R, trail the rest.

wrong.Half at 2R, half at 4R: That is not our plan. The hard rule is a third at 3R.
wrong.All of it at 3R: The last third rides the trail.
wrong.A third each at 1R, 2R and 3R: Trimming that early cuts the runner. The first trim is at 3R.

questions.q: Most Remount trades win small, so cut the runner early to lock in the gain.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Expect most trades to lose. The few runners pay for them, so do not cut the runner early.
questions.lesson_line: Most lose small. The runners pay for the rest.

questions.q: Hold the rest or cash out?
choices: Hold the rest and trail it
Sell it all; a win is a win
Widen the stop to give it room
Add, it is working
questions.answer: Hold the rest and trail it
questions.why: Hold the rest and trail it. Do not cut the runner early. Another third comes off at 5R, then the trail takes the last third.
questions.lesson_line: Let the runner run. The trail does the selling.

wrong.Sell it all; a win is a win: Most trades lose small, so cutting the runner early gives up what pays for the losers.
wrong.Widen the stop to give it room: The stop only moves up, never wider.
wrong.Add, it is working: Full size at one price with one stop. No adding.

questions.story: You sold a third at 3R and moved the stop to breakeven. The stock now sits at 4R, above its 10-day, and you want to cash out.

questions.q: Buy again?
choices: Only on a new trigger, as a new trade
Yes, it is the same setup
Yes, with a wider stop
Yes, at double size
questions.answer: Only on a new trigger, as a new trade
questions.why: Only on a new trigger. A second try is a new trade with its own trigger and stop, at most 3 a week and 6 a month on one stock.
questions.lesson_line: A stop-out is not a signal. Wait for a new trigger.

wrong.Yes, it is the same setup: The same setup is not a trigger. A second try is a new trade with its own trigger and stop.
wrong.Yes, with a wider stop: A wider stop to get back in is the mistake, not the fix.
wrong.Yes, at double size: Doubling to win it back makes a small loss bigger.

questions.story: Your first Remount stopped out. Four sessions later the stock closes back over the 200-day again.

questions.q: Remounts do best while the index still sits under its own 200-day.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Remounts are best after a correction, as the indexes remount their own lines and leaders remount first. They are weak with the index under its own 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: The best Remounts come as the market itself turns up.

questions.q: On a Red market reading we are mostly in cash, so a textbook Remount waits.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Red means mostly cash and shorts. Green is full risk, Yellow is smaller and fewer, and Orange allows only A+ setups.
questions.lesson_line: Red means mostly cash. The setup waits.

questions.q: Take it or pass?
choices: Pass; it is a chop line
Take it; it closed above
Take it at half size
Buy the open tomorrow
questions.answer: Pass; it is a chop line
questions.why: Pass. A flat line that price has crossed back and forth for weeks is a chop line. Weinstein's stage work says to avoid trading the sideways chop.
questions.lesson_line: A flat line crossed for weeks is a chop line. Pass.

wrong.Take it; it closed above: A close above a line it has crossed for weeks proves little. Whipsaw is the main miss.
wrong.Take it at half size: Half size on a chop line is still a chop trade.
wrong.Buy the open tomorrow: Waiting a day does not change a flat, sawed-through line.

questions.story: A stock has crossed back and forth over its flat 200-day for weeks. Today it closes just above the line.

questions.q: Which grades higher?
choices: The one that clears every average
The one with the 50-day overhead
Both grade the same; each is a pass
Neither; both are passes
questions.answer: The one that clears every average
questions.why: The one that clears every average. That is an A plus cue; leaving the 50-day overhead and falling is a B minus cue.
questions.lesson_line: Clear every average at once. That is the A plus picture.

wrong.The one with the 50-day overhead: Leaving the 50-day overhead and falling is a B minus cue.
wrong.Both grade the same; each is a pass: Clearing every average at once is an A plus cue; a falling average overhead is not.
wrong.Neither; both are passes: Both can be taken, and grade sets the size. The weaker one is just a lower grade.

questions.story: Two remounts of the 200-day. One also clears the 20 and 50-day at once. The other leaves the 50-day overhead and falling.

questions.q: What is the call?
choices: Pass; a weak retake on light volume
Buy; the line is retaken on the close
Buy half size and use a tight stop
Buy the next dip back to the line
questions.answer: Pass; a weak retake on light volume
questions.why: Pass. A light-volume reclaim after a heavy-volume break is an invalidation. IBD reads that weak rise as a chance to sell.
questions.lesson_line: Heavy break, light retake: a sell, not a buy.

wrong.Buy; the line is retaken on the close: The line is retaken, but a light-volume reclaim after a heavy-volume break is an invalidation.
wrong.Buy half size and use a tight stop: Half size does not fix a reclaim IBD reads as a sell.
wrong.Buy the next dip back to the line: A dip in a weak retake is no trigger.

questions.story: A stock lost its 50-day on heavy volume. It drifts back over the line on light volume.

questions.q: Remount or U&R?
choices: A U&R, back within 3 sessions
A Remount of the base low
An Oops, a one-session undercut
A 20 EMA pullback to support
questions.answer: A U&R, back within 3 sessions
questions.why: A U&R. An Undercut and Rally closes back above the level within 3 sessions and is bought as the level is retaken.
questions.lesson_line: Back in 3 sessions: a U&R. A long stay under the line: a Remount.

wrong.A Remount of the base low: A Remount lost the line for a long stay. This was a couple of sessions.
wrong.An Oops, a one-session undercut: An Oops is one session that opens under the prior close. This took more than one.
wrong.A 20 EMA pullback to support: A pullback holds its line. This undercut a base low and took it back.

questions.story: The stock closed under its base low on Tuesday. It closed back over it on Thursday.

questions.q: Remount or Oops?
choices: An Oops; it is one session
A Remount of the 50-day line
A Remount of a lost level
An AVWAP reclaim from an event day
questions.answer: An Oops; it is one session
questions.why: An Oops. It is one session. It opens under the prior close, trades under the prior day's low and closes back over the prior close.
questions.lesson_line: One session is an Oops. A lost line takes days.

wrong.A Remount of the 50-day line: A Remount follows a line lost for a long stay. This took one session.
wrong.A Remount of a lost level: No level was lost for days here. One session is an Oops.
wrong.An AVWAP reclaim from an event day: No event day or volume-bent line is described. This was one session.

questions.story: A stock opens under its prior close, trades under yesterday's low and closes back over yesterday's close. All in one session.

questions.q: Which form is this?
choices: The level form of a Remount
A moving-average Remount
A U&R of the breakout level
An AVWAP reclaim from an event
questions.answer: The level form of a Remount
questions.why: The level form of a Remount. A horizontal level that held before it broke, then lost and retaken, is the level form.
questions.lesson_line: Flat level that held, lost, retaken: the level form.

wrong.A moving-average Remount: The line is a breakout level, not the 50-day or the 200-day.
wrong.A U&R of the breakout level: Three weeks under the line is far past a U&R.
wrong.An AVWAP reclaim from an event: A breakout level is flat. The AVWAP bends with volume from an event day.

questions.story: A stock lost its 100.00 breakout level and stayed under it for three weeks. Today it closes back above.

questions.q: Is this a clear remount day?
choices: No; wait for a clear close
Yes, it closed over the line
Yes, buy the next open
Yes, add on strength
questions.answer: No; wait for a clear close
questions.why: No. A close 0.08 ATR over the line is a marginal poke inside the noise. ESS remounted clearly a few sessions later and reached 14.9R.
questions.lesson_line: Wait for the clear close. A poke is not a retake.

wrong.Yes, it closed over the line: A close a hair over the line is a marginal poke inside the noise.
wrong.Yes, buy the next open: Buying a marginal poke is a listed mistake.
wrong.Yes, add on strength: We do not add, and the retake is not clear yet.

questions.story: After weeks under the 50-day, the stock closes 0.08 ATR over it. Nothing else is wrong.

questions.q: Your move before the buy?
choices: Nothing; wait for a new close
Buy anyway; it is just one close
Buy half size, stop at the low
Lower the line and buy
questions.answer: Nothing; wait for a new close
questions.why: Nothing. A close back under the line before the trigger means no trade. The remount is off until it closes above again.
questions.lesson_line: Back under the line before the buy means no trade.

wrong.Buy anyway; it is just one close: A close back under the line before the trigger means no trade.
wrong.Buy half size, stop at the low: Half size does not fix a failed retake.
wrong.Lower the line and buy: Moving the line to fit the chart is how you buy a failed setup.

questions.story: The stock remounted its 200-day yesterday. Today, before you buy, it closes back under the line.

questions.q: Do you buy?
choices: Pass; over 4% above the buy point
Buy; it traded over the high
Buy half size to cut the risk
Buy with a wider stop to fit the gap
questions.answer: Pass; over 4% above the buy point
questions.why: Pass. Never buy more than 4% above the buy point. Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays put and the distance grows.
questions.lesson_line: Four percent over the buy point and I am done.

wrong.Buy; it traded over the high: It did trade over the high, but the fill is more than 4% over the buy point. Never buy more than 4% above the buy point.
wrong.Buy half size to cut the risk: Half of a chase is still a chase.
wrong.Buy with a wider stop to fit the gap: A wider stop to fit a late fill is the mistake, not the fix.

questions.story: The quiet day's high is 50.00. The stock gaps up to 52.60 at the open.

questions.q: Buy over the high?
choices: Pass; more than 10% over the 10-day
Buy; the trigger fired over the high
Buy at half size
Buy and trail it with the 5-day
questions.answer: Pass; more than 10% over the 10-day
questions.why: Pass. Skip a stock that is more than 10% over its 10-day average. The trigger firing does not lift that rule.
questions.lesson_line: More than ten percent over the 10-day: skip.

wrong.Buy; the trigger fired over the high: The trigger fired, and the stretch rule still says no.
wrong.Buy at half size: Smaller size does not make a stretched stock cheaper.
wrong.Buy and trail it with the 5-day: The trail is for exits. The stretch rule is for entries.

questions.story: The quiet day holds above the line. The next morning the stock is 12% over its 10-day average.

questions.q: Buy the close?
choices: No; a report inside 3 sessions
Yes, the picture is perfect
Yes, at half the usual size
Yes, as long as the stop is tight
questions.answer: No; a report inside 3 sessions
questions.why: No. No new buy in the 3 sessions before a report. After the report, a remount on the reaction day itself is allowed.
questions.lesson_line: Report tonight, no buy. After the report, it can trigger.

wrong.Yes, the picture is perfect: The picture is not the issue. No new buys in the 3 sessions before a report.
wrong.Yes, at half the usual size: Half size is still a new buy inside the window.
wrong.Yes, as long as the stop is tight: A tight stop does not lift the earnings rule.

questions.story: A textbook 200-day remount closes today. The company reports earnings tonight.

questions.q: How do you grade it?
choices: B minus; a first try on a curling line
A plus; it finally turned after months
A; it cleared the 50-day on a close
No trade; it is a base
questions.answer: B minus; a first try on a curling line
questions.why: B minus. A first attempt after a long decline, or a line still curling lower, is a B minus cue. Grade sets the size.
questions.lesson_line: First try after a long fall: lower grade, smaller size.

wrong.A plus; it finally turned after months: A first attempt after a long decline is a B minus cue.
wrong.A; it cleared the 50-day on a close: The clear is real, but a line still curling lower is a B minus cue.
wrong.No trade; it is a base: Nothing makes it a base here. It is a lower grade, not a ban.

questions.story: A stock sold off hard for months. Today it remounts its 50-day for the first time, still above its 200-day. The 50-day is still curling lower.

questions.q: What does that add?
choices: An A plus cue: it leads the index
A warning: it is ahead of the market
Nothing; ignore the index
A reason to double size
questions.answer: An A plus cue: it leads the index
questions.why: An A plus cue. A leader that lost the line in a market shakeout and remounted before the index did is an A plus cue.
questions.lesson_line: Leaders remount first. That is the A plus picture.

wrong.A warning: it is ahead of the market: Leaders remount first. That is a cue, not a warning.
wrong.Nothing; ignore the index: The market matters. A leader remounting first is a grade cue.
wrong.A reason to double size: Size comes from the stop and the grade, never doubled.

questions.story: A leader lost its 50-day in a market shakeout. It remounts while the index is still under its own 50-day.

questions.q: Where does that leave you?
choices: Nothing; wait for a fresh trigger
Buy back at 59.54; the line held
Buy now and skip the stop this time
Widen the stop next time
questions.answer: Nothing; wait for a fresh trigger
questions.why: Nothing. The level was right and the trigger did not run. A second try is a new trade with its own trigger and stop.
questions.lesson_line: Right level, wrong trigger. Wait for a new one.

wrong.Buy back at 59.54; the line held: The line held, but the trigger is gone. A second try is a new trade with its own trigger.
wrong.Widen the stop next time: The stop sits under the low it marks. Widening it only makes the loss bigger.

questions.story: You bought at 59.54 with the stop at 58.44. A gap under the stop the next morning ended it. The stock then held its 50-day for 20 sessions.

questions.q: What does this teach?
choices: The stop was the cost of the setup
The stop was set too tight to hold
Never use stops on 200-day names
Buy back at 206.55 on a pullback
questions.answer: The stop was the cost of the setup
questions.why: The stop was the cost of the setup. FDX was a shakeout: stopped the next day, then it reached the 3R level without us.
questions.lesson_line: Some stops are shakeouts. That is the price of the setup.

wrong.The stop was set too tight to hold: It marked the real low. A shakeout through it is the price of the setup.
wrong.Buy back at 206.55 on a pullback: That is chasing. A new try needs its own trigger.

questions.story: You bought a 200-day remount at 198.12 with the stop at 195.31. It stopped you out the next day. Weeks later it reached your old 3R level, 206.55.

questions.q: How do you read this loss?
choices: A planned loss in a weak index
A flaw in the 200-day line itself
A reason to skip stops next time
A sign to buy the gap
questions.answer: A planned loss in a weak index
questions.why: A planned loss. A remount is weak with the index under its own 200-day. AAPL opened lower and traded through the stop the next day.
questions.lesson_line: A clean chart is weak when the index is weak.

wrong.A flaw in the 200-day line itself: The line was fine. The index under its own 200-day made the remount weak.
wrong.A reason to skip stops next time: The stop limits a loss like this. It is never optional.
wrong.A sign to buy the gap: A gap down is not a signal to add.

questions.story: You bought a 200-day remount at 163.43 with the stop at 159.25. The S&P 500 sits under its own 200-day. Next day it opens down at 159.90 and trades through your stop.

questions.q: What did the heavy volume do for the trade?
choices: Nothing; the index was weak
It made the trade an A plus
It removed the need for a stop
It guaranteed follow-through
questions.answer: Nothing; the index was weak
questions.why: Nothing. PYPL remounted its 200-day on the earnings reaction day in the October 2018 correction and stopped out the next session.
questions.lesson_line: Heavy volume does not save a remount in a weak market.

wrong.It made the trade an A plus: The index decides first. PYPL had heavy volume and still stopped out.

questions.story: A 200-day remount shows heavy volume on the earnings reaction day. The index is making new lows. You buy over the quiet day's high.

questions.q: Which one do you buy?
choices: A; clears every average, 2% stop
B; it just retook the 50-day
C; it just closed above the 200-day
None; wait for a better one
questions.answer: A; clears every average, 2% stop
questions.why: A. It clears every average, sits above the 200-day, has a stop under about 3% and a Green reading. B fails the 200-day and C is a chop line.
questions.lesson_line: Context first: above the 200-day, not a chop line, stop inside 3%.

wrong.B; it just retook the 50-day: Under a falling 200-day it is not a buy for us.
wrong.C; it just closed above the 200-day: A flat line crossed ten times is a chop line.
wrong.None; wait for a better one: A is a good one. Waiting for perfect is not the plan.

questions.story: Three charts. A: a leader clears every average, a quiet day, a 2% stop, a Green reading. B: the 50-day retaken under a falling 200-day. C: a flat 200-day crossed ten times.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, an inside day after a strong remount close. Is the 50-day held? Take it or pass?
choices: Take it; the quiet day holds the line
Pass; the close sits under the 50-day
Pass; the remount close was marginal
questions.answer: Take it; the quiet day holds the line
questions.why: Take it. A strong remount close, then an inside day holding above the 50-day. The buy came the next session and 3R the day after.
questions.lesson_line: Strong retake, quiet day above the line: that is the trade.

wrong.Pass; the close sits under the 50-day: Look again: the quiet day closes above the 50-day.
wrong.Pass; the remount close was marginal: The remount close was strong, well clear of the line.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the day it closes back over the 50-day. Where is the close against the 200-day? Take it or pass?
choices: Pass; the close is under the 200-day
Take it; the 50-day was just retaken
Take it; the volume is heavy
questions.answer: Pass; the close is under the 200-day
questions.why: Pass. The reclaim close was 274.51, under the 200-day SMA at 295.88. A 50-day reclaim under the 200-day is a read, not a buy.
questions.lesson_line: A fifty-day retake under the 200-day is not a buy.

wrong.Take it; the 50-day was just retaken: A 50-day reclaim counts only with the close above the 200-day too.
wrong.Take it; the volume is heavy: Volume does not override the 200-day rule.

questions.q: We keep a position under 1% of the stock's average daily volume.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume. Thin stocks are not even on the watchlist.
questions.lesson_line: Stay under 1% of daily volume.

questions.q: After the first third comes off at 3R, where does the stop go?
choices: Up to breakeven, our entry
Down to the line
Up to the quiet day's high
It stays until 5R
questions.answer: Up to breakeven, our entry
questions.why: Up to breakeven. The stop goes to breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default.
questions.lesson_line: First trim off, stop to breakeven.

wrong.Up to the quiet day's high: That is not part of the plan. The stop goes to breakeven, our entry.
wrong.It stays until 5R: Breakeven comes between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Sell a third; the stop goes to breakeven
Sell half; the stop stays
Hold it all; the stop stays
Sell it all
questions.answer: Sell a third; the stop goes to breakeven
questions.why: Sell a third; the stop goes to breakeven. The hard rule is a third at 3R, and the stop moves to breakeven at the first trim by default.
questions.lesson_line: Third off at 3R, stop to breakeven.

wrong.Sell half; the stop stays: The hard rule is a third at 3R. The stop moves to breakeven at the first trim by default.
wrong.Hold it all; the stop stays: The first third comes off at 3R. Holding it all skips the plan.
wrong.Sell it all: The last third rides the trail. Another third comes off at 5R.

questions.story: You bought at 101.19 with the stop at 99.98. The stock trades to 104.82, which is 3R.

questions.q: What is a shakeout below a line meant to do to holders?
choices: Get them to sell to large operators
Lock them in so they ride a rally
Raise the volume for a later breakout
Prove the trend is over
questions.answer: Get them to sell to large operators
questions.why: Get them to sell to large operators. The stock undercuts the line, fakes out sellers and would-be short-sellers, then rallies back above it.
questions.lesson_line: A shakeout shakes out the weak holders. Then the line comes back.

wrong.Lock them in so they ride a rally: A shakeout is meant to get holders out, not lock them in.
wrong.Raise the volume for a later breakout: Volume is a side effect. The aim is to induce selling.
wrong.Prove the trend is over: The undercut fakes out sellers and would-be short-sellers, then rallies back above.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Pass; Orange allows only A plus
Take it at full size
Take it; Orange is Green with a tint
Take it and skip the stop
questions.answer: Pass; Orange allows only A plus
questions.why: Pass. Orange allows only an A+ remount. Green is full risk, Yellow is smaller and fewer, and Red is mostly cash.
questions.lesson_line: Orange means A plus only. A B waits.

wrong.Take it at full size: Full risk is the Green reading. Orange allows only A+ setups.
wrong.Take it; Orange is Green with a tint: Orange is a step down from Yellow. It allows only A+ setups.

questions.story: The market reading is Orange. A Remount sets up cleanly, but you grade it a B.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Hold; the stop is still the exit
Sell at the close; the line failed
Raise the stop to 46.01
Add on the dip
questions.answer: Hold; the stop is still the exit
questions.why: Hold it. A 200-day remount that slips back under the line but stays above the stop is held. The time stop handles the chop.
questions.lesson_line: Slipped under the line, still above the stop: hold.

wrong.Sell at the close; the line failed: A close back under the line is not an extra exit. The stop is the exit.
wrong.Raise the stop to 46.01: The stop moves up with the plan, at the first trim, not on a weak close.
wrong.Add on the dip: Full size at one price with one stop. No adding.

questions.story: You bought a 200-day remount at 46.01 with the stop at 44.80. Three days later it closes at 45.60, back under the 200-day, above your stop.

questions.q: Which grades highest?
choices: B; leader first, all averages clear
A; it finally turned after a long fall
C; it retook the 50-day, rest overhead
All three grade the same
questions.answer: B; leader first, all averages clear
questions.why: B. A leader that remounts before the index is an A plus cue, and so is clearing all the averages at once. A and C are B minus cues.
questions.lesson_line: Leader first, every average cleared: that is the A plus picture.

wrong.A; it finally turned after a long fall: A first attempt after a long decline, or a line still curling lower, is a B minus cue.
wrong.C; it retook the 50-day, rest overhead: A retake that leaves averages overhead and falling is a B minus cue.
wrong.All three grade the same: Grade follows the cues, and these are far apart.

questions.story: Three remounts. A: a first try after a long decline, the line still curling lower. B: a leader that remounts before the index and clears every average. C: the 50-day retaken, other averages overhead and falling.

questions.q: The line is 50.00. The deepest close under it was 48.50. ATR is 1.20. How many ATR under the line?
questions.why: 1.25 ATR. Take the line minus the deepest close, then divide by the ATR. Our card asks for at least 0.5 ATR, so the break left the line.
questions.lesson_line: A real break closes at least half an ATR under the line.

questions.q: Did the break leave the line?
choices: No; the dip stayed under 0.5 ATR
Yes; any close under the line is a break
Yes; the close back over proves it
No; it needs a close under the 200-day
questions.answer: No; the dip stayed under 0.5 ATR
questions.why: No. Our card asks that at least one close sat 0.5 ATR or more under the line. This dip reached only 0.2 ATR.
questions.lesson_line: A dip inside the noise is not a lost line. Wait for a real break.

wrong.Yes; any close under the line is a break: One close under the line is not enough. Our card wants one at least 0.5 ATR under it.
wrong.Yes; the close back over proves it: The close back over is the retake. The break must be deep enough first.
wrong.No; it needs a close under the 200-day: The 200-day is a separate test. This one is about how deep the dip went under the 50-day.

questions.story: A stock held its 50-day for months. It dipped under on a few closes, the deepest only 0.2 ATR below the line. Today it closes back over.

questions.q: A price level counts as a Remount line only if the stock held it before the break.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Our card wants a level that held before it broke. At least 10 of the 15 closes before the break were at or above it.
questions.lesson_line: A level has to hold before it can be lost.

questions.q: Is 80.00 a real level for a Remount?
choices: No; too few closes were above it
Yes; the retake is what counts
Yes; any round number is a level
No; a Remount uses averages only
questions.answer: No; too few closes were above it
questions.why: No. Our card wants a level that held before it broke, at least 10 of the 15 closes at or above it. Here only 5 did.
questions.lesson_line: Chopping through a price for weeks does not make it a level.

wrong.Yes; the retake is what counts: The retake comes second. The level has to have held before the break.
wrong.Yes; any round number is a level: A round number counts only if it held. Weeks of chop through it says it did not.
wrong.No; a Remount uses averages only: The level form is real. A price level that held before it broke counts.

questions.story: A stock breaks under 80.00 and later closes back over it. In the 15 sessions before the break, only 5 closes were at or above 80.00. It had chopped through that price for weeks.

questions.q: What is our card's variant buy?
choices: Buy as it turns positive on the day
Buy the open to catch the dip
Wait for a close over the prior high
Skip it; a gap down ends the setup
questions.answer: Buy as it turns positive on the day
questions.why: Buy as it turns positive on the day. On a gap down that stays above the line, our card buys the turn. The stop goes under that day's low.
questions.lesson_line: Gap down, line held: buy the turn to positive.

wrong.Buy the open to catch the dip: The open is the weakest moment. The variant waits for price to turn positive.
wrong.Wait for a close over the prior high: That waits for the daily close. This variant buys the turn on the day itself.
wrong.Skip it; a gap down ends the setup: A gap down that stays above the line is the case this variant is for.

questions.story: Yesterday was a clean remount day. Today the stock gaps down at the open but stays above the line. You have not bought yet.

questions.q: A Remount can be timed on the hourly chart, on a higher low or a flag.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Our card teaches the hourly timing, a higher low or a flag, as a variant. Daily drills cannot show it.
questions.lesson_line: Hourly timing is a variant. The daily rules stay the base.

questions.q: Do you add to the position?
choices: No; one price, one stop, no adds
Yes; add half with the same stop
Yes; add, and move the stop to average
No; sell half to lock in the gain
questions.answer: No; one price, one stop, no adds
questions.why: No. We buy the full size at one price with one stop, and no adding. The course teaches one entry.
questions.lesson_line: One entry, one price, one stop. Liking it more is not a trigger.

wrong.Yes; add half with the same stop: Half now and half later is two entries. We buy the full size at one price.
wrong.Yes; add, and move the stop to average: Moving the stop to fit an add breaks the one-stop rule.
wrong.No; sell half to lock in the gain: Trims come at 3R and 5R, a third each. Half now is not the plan.

questions.story: You bought a Remount at 40.00 with the stop at 38.80. Two days later it holds the line again on a quiet day. You like it even more.

questions.q: Bought at 59.54 with the stop at 58.44. Where is 5R?
questions.why: 65.04. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add five of those to the fill. The second third comes off there.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 5R before the open. The second third comes off there.

questions.q: What comes off at 5R?
choices: Another 100; trail the last 100
The other 200; no trail needed
Another 50; trail the other 150
Nothing; wait for the 21-day
questions.answer: Another 100; trail the last 100
questions.why: Another 100, a third of the position. After the first third at 3R comes another third at 5R, then you trail the last third.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, a third at 5R, then the trail.

wrong.The other 200; no trail needed: The plan keeps the last third on the trail. A third comes off at 5R, not all of it.
wrong.Another 50; trail the other 150: Half a third is not the plan. The second trim is a third of the position.
wrong.Nothing; wait for the 21-day: The trail is for the last third, after both trims. At 5R the second third comes off.

questions.story: You hold 300 shares of a Remount. You sold 100 at 3R. Today the stock reaches 5R.

questions.q: May you take the fourth try?
choices: No; three tries a week is the limit
Yes; every trigger is a new trade
No; two tries a week is the limit
Yes; if the stop is wider this time
questions.answer: No; three tries a week is the limit
questions.why: No. A new trigger after a failed try is a new trade. But the cap is 3 tries a week and 6 a month on one stock.
questions.lesson_line: A new trigger is a new trade, but the cap still holds.

wrong.Yes; every trigger is a new trade: A new trigger is a new trade, but there is a cap: 3 tries a week on one stock.
wrong.No; two tries a week is the limit: The cap is 3 tries a week and 6 a month on one stock.
wrong.Yes; if the stop is wider this time: A wider stop is never the fix. The stop only moves up.

questions.story: This week you took three Remount tries on one stock. All three hit the stop. Today it triggers a fourth time.

questions.q: After a stop-out, a second Remount try is a new trade with its own trigger and its own stop.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. After a stop-out, buy again only if the setup triggers again, as a new trade with its own stop.
questions.lesson_line: A second try is a new trade, not a rescue.

questions.q: Which carries the stronger A plus cue?
choices: B; average and level together
A; one clean line reads better
Same; a second line adds nothing
A; a level only adds noise to it
questions.answer: B; average and level together
questions.why: B. On our card a line many people watch is an A plus cue, best when an average and a level sit together. It is a cue, not a score.
questions.lesson_line: An average and a level together: the strongest line to retake.

wrong.A; one clean line reads better: Two lines taken back at once is the stronger picture, not the noisier one.
wrong.Same; a second line adds nothing: A second line that many people watch adds to the cue.
wrong.A; a level only adds noise to it: A round number is a level many people name. Together with an average it is the best case.

questions.story: Two remounts close back over their line today. A retakes the 50-day alone. B retakes the 50-day and the round 100.00 level together.

questions.q: How does the report change the trade?
choices: Allowed; it counts as a B minus cue
Blocked; no buys within 10 sessions
Allowed; it is an A plus catalyst
Blocked; no buys within 8 sessions
questions.answer: Allowed; it counts as a B minus cue
questions.why: Allowed, as a B minus cue. A report within about two weeks (10 sessions) lowers the grade. Only the 3 sessions before are barred.
questions.lesson_line: A report close by lowers the grade. Only the last 3 sessions bar the buy.

wrong.Blocked; no buys within 10 sessions: Only the 3 sessions before a report are barred. Ten sessions is a cue, not a ban.
wrong.Allowed; it is an A plus catalyst: A report close by lowers the grade. It does not raise it.
wrong.Blocked; no buys within 8 sessions: Only the 3 sessions before a report are barred. Eight sessions is outside that.
